claim: Warhol v. Goldsmith (2023, 7–2) held the first factor disfavored the Warhol Foundation because its commercial licensing of "Orange Prince" shared substantially the same purpose as Goldsmith's photograph.
evidence: U.S. Supreme Court holds that first factor in fair use analysis, “the purpose and character of the use, including whether such use is of a commercial nature or is for nonprofit educational purposes,” does not support fair use defense for Andy Warhol Foundation’s licensing of silkscreen print of pop icon Prince that was based on black-and-white photograph, because original photograph and AWF’s use had substantially similar purposes, and use was commercial.
